speaker: Doctor
text: I see you are an 8-month-old boy experiencing feeding difficulties and abdominal distension. To understand what is happening inside you, have you been vomiting, and if so, has it ever looked like it contained green or yellow fluid?

speaker: Patient
text: The baby has been very fussy, feeding less than usual, and the abdomen looks distended. Crying gets worse when the belly is touched.

speaker: Doctor
text: That touching of the belly causes significant pain, which often points to an obstruction or severe inflammation. Have you noticed any "currant jelly" stools or any blood in the stool recently? Also, when the baby vomits, does the belly feel very hard or tense at the same time?

speaker: Patient
text: There has not been fever, vomiting, or diarrhea like a stomach infection. The baby was born at 39 weeks without birth complications.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Given the lack of vomiting or bloody stools, we need to rule out anatomical causes like a distal intestinal obstruction. Please confirm if the baby has passed meconium within the first 24 hours of life, and has he had any episodes of explosive, foul-smelling stools since then?

REQUEST TEST: Abdominal_X-Ray

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Abdominal_X-Ray: Dilated bowel segments with absence of gas in the rectum, suggesting a possible obstruction; Abdominal_Ultrasound: Normal readings

speaker: Doctor
text:
Based on the X-ray showing dilated bowel segments and absent gas in the rectum, does the baby have a history of chronic, foul-smelling, greasy stools or significant failure to gain weight?

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Distal Intestinal Obstruction (likely Distal Intestinal Obstruction Syndrome or atresia) based on X-ray findings of dilated bowel and absent rectal gas, despite normal ultrasound and meconium ileus screening.
